A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GATEAU study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–J support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark results, ablations, and human evaluations in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds LLaMA-3 and LongAlpaca experiments in Appendix I.

M1.justification: HMG, CAM, weighted sample ranking, and the SFT objective remain unchanged in Equations (1)–(7). Updated illustrative checkpoints and additional backbone evaluations do not alter the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v5 adds LongAlpaca as a second long-instruction training corpus, containing 9,000 samples (Appendix I.3). LongAlign, ShareGPT, the evaluation benchmarks, and their task and language coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Cherry Selection, CaR, Perplexity Guidance, and the existing training controls remain in their corresponding comparisons. The added experiments reuse the Full-100% control without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: v5 adds LLaMA-3-8B evaluations using 8k/64k homologous checkpoints and 50% data selection, plus 50%-versus-full training on LongAlpaca. These extend experimental configurations; the existing budgets, metrics, and two short-instruction-data settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, parameter sweeps, needle-retrieval tests, OOD case study, diversity analysis, and mixed-quality analysis are retained. The new tables extend benchmark comparisons across backbones and training corpora rather than introduce a distinct ablation or robustness-testing procedure.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the stated practice of averaging two GPT-4 scoring passes. No training-seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 7–8 in v5 add supporting results while retaining all matched earlier numerical results. Under real-world settings, the added LLaMA-3 experiment reports LongBench-Chat scores of 65.3 versus 54.4 for full-data training; the LongAlpaca experiment reports 50.2 versus 45.6. These are additional experiments, not improvements over v3 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The mathematical score definitions, normalization, attention aggregation, training objective, and diversity-selection formulation remain equivalent. No substantive mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: selecting samples rich in long-range dependencies through HMG and CAM improves alignment with less long-instruction data. The additional experiments support this existing contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: New Appendix I.3 interprets the LongAlpaca results as evidence that GATEAU generalizes across long-instruction training datasets. Existing mechanism explanations and the three stated limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: The new Lian (2024) reference supplies a checkpoint-source link for LLaMA-3-8B-64k-PoSE. Appendix A's training recipe, hardware specifications, execution-time reporting, and the promised GATEAU code/data/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Grattafiori et al. (2024) and Lian (2024) for LLaMA-3 and removes Together.ai (2023). The positioning against short-instruction data-selection research remains unchanged; the LongAlpaca-related LongLoRA work was already cited.

P1.justification: v5 makes grammatical and wording edits throughout, renames Section 3.2 from 'Impact of GATEAU' to 'Main Results,' and inserts Appendix I.3 with subsequent subsection renumbering. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 uses revised LLM illustrations, Table 7 gains LLaMA-3 rows, and a new Table 8 presents LongAlpaca results. Several prompt displays are repaginated and captions standardized; the existing empirical plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Adding LLaMA-3 and a second long-instruction training corpus provides broader empirical support than v3's LongAlign-centered evaluation while preserving its existing results and analyses. The gain is limited: the added experiments compare against full-data training and provide no additional uncertainty reporting.
